title: Request tab
summary: Choose fixed rates, maximise output, or use Satisfactory mode to balance production by item tier.
body:
Press **+ Add Item** and choose what you want to produce. Each row has a rate selector: a fixed amount per minute, **maximise**, **Satisfactory mode**, or **Satisfactory+ mode**. New item requests start in Satisfactory+ mode. Set the available materials and limits in [Resources](help:tab-resources), and choose allowed recipes in [Recipes](help:tab-recipes). The calculation shares resources and intermediate production across all requested items.

## Power production

Choose **Power (generators)** in the item dropdown to plan electricity production. On its own it starts in **maximise** mode; alongside automatic item requests it joins their Satisfactory mode. It uses the available fuel and supplemental resources such as water. On a new plan, generator fuels are enabled automatically; change the allowed fuels in the **Power** tab. Existing fuel selections are preserved. Set supplied materials in **Inputs** and mining limits in **Resources**, just as for item production. Disable mining resources if the plan should use only supplied inputs.

**Power takes precedence in combined plans.** Automatic basic item targets reserve the output of **two full machines at 100%** instead of consuming all resources to maximise materials. The calculation then maximises power while preserving those material outputs. Set a custom Satisfactory item rate to choose a different reservation. Satisfactory+ keeps production machines and generators at 100% with whole counts. For example, with standard recipes, **720 oil/min** can support **40 plastic/min**, **40 rubber/min** and **5,500 MW** from **22 fuel generators**. The complete factory is solved together, so heavy oil residue can become fuel and every resource limit still applies.

The graph connects fuel and water supplies to generators and shows their count and power output. At 100% clock speed, **480 coal/min and 1,440 water/min** support **32 coal generators producing 2,400 MW**. With only **1,000 water/min**, water limits output to about **1,666.67 MW**. Use a fixed MW, GW or TW target when you want a specific amount instead.

## Fixed rates

Choose **/min** and enter the amount you want to keep as a final output each minute, in addition to anything consumed by other requested items. Fluids use m³/min. Fixed item targets can be combined with automatic or maximised item targets; fixed targets reserve their resources first.

## Maximise

Choose **maximise** to produce as much as the available resources, supplied inputs and enabled recipes allow. For example, use it to find how much aluminium a limited bauxite supply can produce. With several maximised items, the calculation raises their output together, then continues with items that can still grow after another reaches its limit.

Fixed targets and maximised targets can be mixed. A request for 300 plates/min plus maximised rods reserves production for the plates first, then uses the remaining capacity for rods. The result appears in the rate field after calculation.

:::warning
Maximising with somersloops can take much longer. Try calculating without sloops first.
:::

## Satisfactory mode

Satisfactory mode favours modest amounts of advanced parts and larger amounts of basic materials, while staying within the resources you have provided.

- **Space Elevator parts:** aim for the output of two machines at 100%, such as **4 Smart Plating/min** or **10 Versatile Framework/min**. Enabled standard recipes take priority over alternates for these parts. If the standard recipe is disabled or unavailable, an enabled alternate can be used.
- **The top two other production tiers:** aim for twice the recipe's output batch.
- **Intermediate parts:** aim for about five recipe batches per minute. A recipe producing two Modular Frames therefore targets **10 Modular Frames/min**.
- **Basic materials:** share the remaining resources to maximise their output.

Automatic targets are reserved in production hierarchy order and may reduce, including to zero, when resources are short. The calculation then simplifies the production chain for a factory built with manifolds. It favours whole internal material rates, then halves and tenths, with straightforward machine clocks as a secondary preference. Final outputs can retain more decimal places when that makes the rest of the factory simpler.

Each automatic output may decrease by up to **2%** from its initially calculated rate. Basic outputs can also increase by up to 2% to find a better combination; advanced outputs stay within their preferred targets. Outputs below 0.1/min stay unchanged. Custom rates remain exact. A small amount of unused resource capacity and a few extra machines are acceptable. The Resources tab shows used and unused mining capacity.

Simplification adjusts the actual production plan using the selected production routes; it does not just round the display or design balanced splitters. It has a short time limit and keeps the original valid factory if a simpler result cannot be found.

For power and AWESOME Sink points, Satisfactory mode maximises the result and then rebuilds at a clean rate.

### Custom rates in Satisfactory mode

Edit a rate and leave the field to keep that output fixed. The row is marked **Custom**, and the other automatic outputs recalculate around it. For example, set Reinforced Iron Plates to **15/min** to reserve that output before allocating the remaining materials. Advanced automatic targets stay at their preferred rates when enough resources remain.

Choose **Reset to auto** to let Satisfactory mode manage the row again. Custom rates stay exactly as entered; if they cannot fit within your resource limits, the calculation cannot produce a valid plan.

## Satisfactory+ mode

Satisfactory+ uses the same tier targets and round-rate preferences as Satisfactory mode, and uses whole machines at **100%** for requested products and generators. Unrequested intermediate machines may underclock during allocation so rounding them up does not starve requested outputs. A final cleanup pass clocks down excess production of unrequested intermediate items and reduces their upstream supply. Removing avoidable byproducts takes priority over round clocks in this pass, while requested product totals stay unchanged. It overrides configured machine and generator clocks for this calculation. Choose **Satisfactory+ mode** from the rate selector.

Whole machines take priority over resource utilisation. Resource capacity may remain unused, and exact custom rates or recipe batch sizes may leave surplus output. Surplus of a requested item is included in its green product total; unrequested intermediate surplus is removed by underclocking wherever the selected recipes and locked machines allow. Unavoidable co-products can remain visible as byproducts. Custom rates remain exact; when whole machines cannot fit your resource limits, the plan may be infeasible. Locked production machines must have whole counts and clocks between 1% and 100%; locked generators must run at 100%. Integer optimisation can take longer than ordinary Satisfactory mode.

## Removing

Use the cross at the end of a row to remove that request.
